terms.comment: A description of ours, in Vergil’s words: in verubus torrēre is to roast on spits (Verg. G. 2.396). We have found no name for such a dish in Traupman, Morgan–Owens, or Levi–Bini, and have not Latinised the local name.
The skewer itself. The ablative plural is verubus, or veribus in Vergil.

phrases.latin: Pater frusta pullī in verubus super carbōnēs torret.
phrases.english: Daddy is roasting bits of chicken on skewers over the coals.

phrases.latin: pars in frusta secant veribusque trementia fīgunt
phrases.english: some cut the meat into pieces and fix them, still quivering, on spits

phrases.latin: pinguiaque in veribus torrēbimus exta colurnīs
phrases.english: and we shall roast the rich entrails on spits of hazel

sources: Lewis & Short: veru · Lewis & Short: torreo
